Why the wealthy set their targets low first.

Kevin Trudeau tells of a man whose team sets targets sky high and never hits them. Kevin disagrees. He says success builds confidence, so you set the rules so you win.

He compares it to a quarterback who throws a short pass first to get momentum. Beat an early target, set the next one, and the wins start to stack up.

When did a small win last change how you felt about the next step?

#ad #success #goals #mindset

Why success looks easy but takes hard work.

Kevin Trudeau says the idea that everything should come easy is fantasy island. He points out that people with huge wealth work extremely hard. They wake up early, go to bed late and don't sit around waiting for money to flow in.

The difference, Kevin says, is that they love it. For them the journey is the reward.

What would you work this hard for, simply because you love it?

#ad #success #habits #mindset

Why most people never use the courses they buy.

Kevin Trudeau tells of a famous real estate course that works if you apply it. Most buyers shoved the tapes under the bed. Others started and quit, and others listened to them all and said they would start tomorrow.

Kevin calls this a counter intention, a block that leads to self-sabotage of success.

What is one thing you keep saying you will start tomorrow?

#ad #success #mindset #habits

How two words stopped a bad driving habit.

Kevin Trudeau tells how he moved house and kept driving to the old one on autopilot. The next time he caught himself halfway and said two words: cancel, cancel. By the third trip he told himself, I know where I live.

He says that is how you break a counter intention or a bad habit, and it starts with awareness.

What habit do you run on autopilot?
